findings.problem: The 30s cold-start diagnostic snapshot is skipped entirely if the first pidof call throws (app process dead at 30s — pidof exits 1 and execFileSync throws), so a crash during the earliest Hermes window produces no COLD-START [30s] log line. This is a minor diagnostic gap, not a functional defect: the waitFor app-alive check (every 30s) and the timeout diagnostics (pidof + logcat + dumpsys + UI dump) still capture the crash evidence.
findings.evidence: launch() wraps the whole snapshot in try/catch (_) {}; shell('pidof', packageName) throws on exit 1 (no process), skipping the dumpsys/logcat capture; the existing app-alive check in waitFor handles err.status === 1 explicitly and relaunches.
findings.requiredFix: None required for acceptance. Optional hardening for a future cycle: split the pidof check from the dumpsys/logcat capture so a dead process still logs 'COLD-START [30s]: app process pid=NOT FOUND' and captures logcat for the crash reason.
findings.verification: The waitFor app-alive check and timeout diagnostics already capture crash evidence; the Demarrer wait diagnostics (every 120s) will show pid=NOT FOUND if the app dies mid-wait.

findings.problem: The mid-wait logcat call uses adb(['logcat', '-d', '-t', '60'], { timeoutMs: 10_000 }) with the default retries=3 and allowReconnect=true, so a logcat timeout could trigger adbReconnect (kill-server + start-server, ~10s) inside a wait loop. This is consistent with existing patterns (the app-alive pidof check and the timeout logcat capture use the same defaults) and bounded (10s timeout, 120s cadence), so it does not materially threaten the Demarrer 900s window.
findings.evidence: adb() default retries=3 with allowReconnect=true; the same pattern already exists at line 532 (app-alive pidof) and line 663 (timeout logcat); adbReconnect is the script's established recovery mechanism for degraded transport.
findings.requiredFix: None required for acceptance. Optional refinement: pass { retries: 1, allowReconnect: false } to the diagnostic logcat/dumpsys calls so diagnostics can never trigger a reconnect.
findings.verification: Diagnostics are read-only and bounded; the wait deadline is wall-clock based, so at most ~10s per 120s window is consumed in the worst case.
